The test image shows a corn ear with white/grayish-white mold covering multiple kernels. Key observations:
- White to grayish-white cottony/fluffy mold
- Mold covers a band of kernels on the ear
- Some slight greenish tinge in areas
- Yellow healthy kernels visible around the affected area

This points to an ear rot. Candidates: Diplodia (white mold from base), Gibberella (red/pink from tip), Aspergillus (olive-green), Trichoderma (dark green), Fusarium (salmon-pink starburst). The white mold is most consistent with Diplodia or potentially Gibberella. Let me check reference images.

The Fusarium reference (top-right) shows a concentrated patch of white/cottony mold on yellow kernels, closely matching the test image. The Diplodia reference shows dried/mummified brown ears, not this fluffy white mold. Let me confirm with two more references.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image**: White/gray-white fluffy, cottony mold concentrated on a band of kernels; surrounding kernels are yellow and healthy
- **Fusarium reference (top-right panel)**: Nearly identical — concentrated white/cottony mold patch on yellow kernels, same distribution pattern
- **Diplodia reference**: Shows late-stage dried/mummified brown ears — no fluffy white mold visible
- **Gibberella reference**: Shows reddish/dark husk symptoms, not matching
- **Aspergillus reference**: Olive-green to gray-green powdery mold — color doesn't match
- **Trichoderma reference**: Dark green mold — clearly doesn't match
- **Common smut**: Large greenish-white galls — completely different

The white cottony mold concentrated in a section of the ear with healthy yellow kernels around it aligns most closely with Fusarium ear rot. The Fusarium reference collage's top-right image is visually nearly identical to the test image.
